ratings.comment: Professor Jones cares about all his students and is always open to hearing new suggestions about how to make the class more accessible. He isn't very hard on attendance, which is nice considering the class is three times a week. Sometimes as an instructor he can talk in circles which makes it hard to understand the class content.

Very knowledgeable and caring of students. Is a very nice grader. However, he articulates in circles and obfuscates content beyond necessity, making his lectures unlistenable. 50% participation, 2 tests and an essay. All of which are easy although unclear. Attendance is effectively mandatory as he a small assignment each class. Pretty ok overall.

While the content of the class was a bit confusing a lot of the time, Jones made the lectures engaging and interesting. He taught in a way that let students think about the material in their own way, not introducing one specific answer but facilitating discussion that allowed for many ideas to be talked about.

Prof Jones is a kind and reasonable guy; he's extremely smart in his field. Sometimes, there is a disconnect between the material he teaches in lecture and our actual assignments. Honestly, I don't think you NEED to go to lecture to know what you need to do for hw. The big grades in the class are writing assignments. Prof will help you if you need.

The lectures are soooooo boring. But you need to go to because he assigns reading quizzes and you need an access code for them. Besides papers, which there's only really only 3, everything is completion. Discussion posts, reading quizzes, are all completion. He's a very sweet person and it seems like he cares about you learning stuff than grades.

Prof. Jones seems like a nice guy, but his lectures are so boring and unengaging that it was really difficult to get into the subject material. He talks very slow and his presentations don't seem to have much structure or thought put into them.

Professor Jones is genuinely so cool and such a nice guy! He opens up the floor for students to share their ideas, and never tries to force the class to one specific conclusion. Its also cool when he mentions his own interests - he seems to be a role model for kids with niche/geeky interests like me to go on and do great things!

Jones is a really great guy that makes this class pretty easy to pass. Your grades come from two short papers and two projects that take no more than an hour, as well as a lecture attendance question. The papers are graded lightly and you're not assessed on your knowledge on any of the readings. Interesting and fairly easy class for a humanity req.
